title: Finite-index transfer on continuous cochain complexes
statement:
Let $E$ be a topological field [def-weil-field], $G$ a profinite group, $H\subseteq G$ an open subgroup, and $V$ a topological $E$-vector space with continuous $E$-linear $G$-action. For a topological group $J$ and a topological $E$-vector space $V$ with continuous linear $J$-action define the ordinary nonnegative complex $C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(J,V)=C(J^n,V)$ of abstract $E$-vector spaces, with $C^0_{\mathrm{cts}}(J,V)=V$ and differential
$$(df)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n).$$
For $n=0$ this reads $(dv)(g)=gv-v$. Cohomology means kernel modulo image in abstract $E$-vector spaces, with no closure of the coboundaries. Restriction is the cochain map $\mathrm{res}:C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V)$. There exists an $E$-linear cochain map
$$\mathrm{cor}:C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V)\longrightarrow C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V)$$
whose composite $\mathrm{cor}\,\mathrm{res}$ is cochain-homotopic to $[G:H]\,\mathrm{id}$. The homotopy consists of $E$-linear maps between these spaces of continuous functions. The construction can be made simultaneously natural in continuous $G$-equivariant $E$-linear maps of coefficient spaces: such maps commute with $\mathrm{cor}$ and with the homotopy. Thus a closed $G$-stable coefficient subspace is preserved by transfer when the transfer is constructed for it and for $V$ using the same coset representatives. No completeness or local compactness of $V$ and no discreteness of its topology are required.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates] for $J=G,H$, with the subspace topology and restricted action on $H$. Its derived isomorphism is represented by actual mutually inverse cochain maps $\Phi_J,\Psi_J$ between the homogeneous complex $B_J$ and the specified inhomogeneous complex. Use these actual maps. Its restriction identity is $R\Psi_G=\Psi_H\mathrm{res}$ for homogeneous restriction $R:B_G\to B_H$. The restricted action is jointly continuous by composition with the subgroup inclusion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-coset-homogeneous-averaging] to compact $G$ and open $H$. Choose its finite transversal $S$ once, independently of the coefficient space. It supplies $r$, the continuous maps $a_s(x)=s^{-1}r(sx)$ and the natural cochain map $T:B_H\to B_G$. Its composite formula identifies $TR$ with $L_nF=\sum_s F(a_s(x_0),\ldots,a_s(x_n))$, and $|S|=[G:H]$.

proof.text: The permutations and covariance $a_s(ax)=a a_{\pi_a(s)}(x)$ supplied by [lem-sfb-finite-coset-homogeneous-averaging] satisfy exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-equivariant-continuous-cochain-prism]. Apply it to obtain continuous-valued, $E$-linear, $G$-equivariant $K_n$ with $\delta K+K\delta=L-|S|\,\mathrm{id}=TR-[G:H]\,\mathrm{id}$, including degree zero. Its coefficient naturality holds for this same family $(a_s)$.

proof.text: Set $\mathrm{cor}=\Phi_G T\Psi_H$ and $k_n=\Phi_{G,n-1}K_n\Psi_{G,n}$ for $n\geq1$, with $k_0=0$. The actual cochain identities of [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates] give, in degree $n\geq0$, $$d_{n-1}k_n+k_{n+1}d_n=\Phi_{G,n}(\delta_{n-1}K_n+K_{n+1}\delta_n)\Psi_{G,n}=\Phi_{G,n}T_nR_n\Psi_{G,n}-[G:H]\,\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{cor}_n\mathrm{res}_n-[G:H]\,\mathrm{id}.$$ Here degree $-1$ is zero, $R_n\Psi_{G,n}=\Psi_{H,n}\mathrm{res}_n$, and $\Phi_{G,n}\Psi_{G,n}=\mathrm{id}$. Composition of cochain maps also makes $\mathrm{cor}$ a cochain map. Every factor is linear with values in continuous functions. For a continuous equivariant linear coefficient map $b$, the coordinate naturality and the naturalities of [lem-sfb-finite-coset-homogeneous-averaging] and [lem-sfb-equivariant-continuous-cochain-prism] commute $b$ through every factor of $\mathrm{cor}$ and $k$. Choose the same $S,r,(a_s)$ for all coefficients. A stable subspace $U\subseteq V$ has a continuous restricted action by its subspace topology; its inclusion gives preservation, in particular for closed $U$. No additional coefficient-topology hypothesis is used.
